chunks: ʿUthmān ibn ʿĪsā, from Samāʿah, said:
I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, “How much is the blood money of a dhimmī?” He said: “Eight hundred dirhams.”

key_terms.الذِّمِّيِّ: a non-Muslim living under Muslim covenant and protection
key_terms.دِرْهَمٍ: dirhams; a unit of silver currency used for legal valuation
key_terms.دِيَةُ: blood money; the prescribed financial compensation for unlawful killing or injury

ai.seo_question: What is the diyah of a dhimmī according to Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith records a legal ruling from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام concerning the diyah of a dhimmī. It states that the prescribed amount is eight hundred dirhams, making it a concise jurisprudential text in the area of judicial and financial law.
